solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unconcerned about English lacking vehicle

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps itself round the other

parts.note: without a car, so car plus the suffix meaning lacking
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't drive shrugs off any worry about English matters.
explanation.walkthrough: CARLESS goes about E, giving CAR(E)LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless person pays little attention or shows no worry, which is being unconcerned.

clue.text: Repeated tea dance

wordplay.note: cha is an informal British word for tea, and repeated means it is written twice

explanation.surface: A tea dance held over and over again.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha (from Chinese) is old British slang for tea, as in 'a cup of cha'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom step of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Set up again controls on giant

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: reins are the straps used to control a horse
a giant is very tall

explanation.surface: Someone restores the controls on a huge machine after a fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstall software or equipment is to put it in place once more after removal.

clue.text: A star of the stage I partnered with Laurel over nice dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, so the words before are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stage performer boasts of partnering Laurel (of Laurel and Hardy) in a nice dance routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partnered with Laurel' suggests Hardy, but Laurel is only letters to shuffle with I, OVER and NICE into LAURENCE OLIVIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was one of the most celebrated British theatre actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Maiden and male in perhaps costumes and crowns

indicators.note: in places the first items inside the outer word

parts.note: costumes are an example of suits of clothes, hence perhaps
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A girl and a man dressed in costumes and wearing crowns, as at a pageant.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden is an over in cricket with no runs scored; 'perhaps' marks costumes as one example of the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Summits are the highest points of hills, just as crowns are the tops of heads or hills.

clue.text: Fruit drinks with postage & packaging added in

indicators.note: added in means put inside, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: ales are beers
p&p is the usual abbreviation for postage and packing on mail orders

explanation.surface: An online order of fruit drinks, with delivery charges tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: Postage and packing is the British term for a shipping charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Apples are common orchard produce, a familiar kind of fruit.

clue.text: Absurdly arrogant ones pan Caesar's unwelcome sort

indicators.note: absurdly suggests things set out in a nonsensical order, so the letters need rearranging

parts.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Conceited critics savage the emperor's least welcome guest.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar's points to Latin, the language of the answer phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Persona non grata is Latin for an unacceptable person, someone officially unwelcome, typically a diplomat expelled.

clue.text: Run out of recent drink

indicators.note: out of means taken away from, so the first item is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: the latter part is the more recent
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: We've run out of the drink we bought recently.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R from LATTER to leave LATTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an espresso coffee with plenty of steamed milk.

clue.text: Investigation possibly turns icy

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements of the letters that follow

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An inquiry may chill the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close critical examination, which is what an inquiry or probe involves.

clue.text: Go on to say drink makes sense

parts.note: to add is to say something further
to sup is to sip or drink

explanation.surface: Someone continues talking, insisting that a drink would be sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: When a story adds up it is logical and consistent, so it is reasonable.

clue.text: Macron's valediction fail in a university

indicators.note: in puts the first word inside the pair of letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written
to die is to fail, as an engine does
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: The French president says goodbye after failing at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: DIE sits inside A and U: A(DIE)U. Macron, the French president, signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French farewell, so it is what a French speaker says when parting.

clue.text: Who keeps an eye on unsettled dear in estate?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the next one

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, a motor

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the following word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Who watches over a troubled loved one on a country estate?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate' suggests land, but it is an estate car, a British station wagon, and so a car in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A moderator oversees a debate, forum or exam, supervising so that rules are followed.

clue.text: Fits of laughter as dodgy lawyer in charge succeeded changing sides

indicators.note: succeeded is S, and changing sides moves that letter from the front to the back

parts.note: a shyster is an unscrupulous lawyer
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer's success has onlookers in fits of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: SHYSTER + IC gives SHYSTERIC; its opening S (succeeded) then moves to the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysterics can mean uncontrollable laughter, as in 'had the audience in hysterics'.

clue.text: Apparent excess beginning from this

parts.note: an excess is an amount over

indicators.note: beginning picks out only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the first letter of this

explanation.surface: An apparent surplus starts from here.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means openly visible, done without concealment, so plain or evident.

clue.text: Ticket prices stuck by clubs producing comedies

indicators.note: stuck by means pierced by, so the second item is pushed into the first

parts.note: fares are the prices of travel tickets
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Fixed ticket prices at nightclubs turn into a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: C is pushed into FARES: FAR(C)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Farces are broad stage comedies built on improbable situations and slapstick.

clue.text: Jug for the innocent to revel in

definitions.text: Jug for the innocent to revel in

parts.note: to revel is to make merry, to play
jug is slang for prison, and a pen is an enclosure or prison

explanation.surface: A jail where babies are locked up so they can have fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, while 'Jug' and 'revel' supply the two parts. Jug is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A playpen is a small enclosure where an infant can amuse itself safely, a cot-sized prison for babies.

clue.text: Dot over 'i' — this is what you see in deli, say

definitions.text: what you see in deli, say

parts.note: to pepper is to dot or sprinkle
on can mean over, upon
taken as written

explanation.surface: A handwriting lesson: put a dot over the letter i, as on a deli sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot over i' reads as a penmanship tip, but it is a verb, a preposition and a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-style salami, typical stock on a delicatessen counter.

clue.text: Butcher's service? Superb, King admitted

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the second item goes inside the word before it

parts.note: ace means excellent
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop offers excellent service, as the king has conceded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' reads as a shop, but the 's is short for 'is', linking the verb definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre people is to slaughter them brutally, which is what butcher means as a verb.

clue.text: Everything mentioned in total

parts.note: all means everything
told means related or mentioned

explanation.surface: Every item has been listed in the total.
explanation.definitionFit: All told is an idiom meaning altogether, when everything is counted.

clue.text: Germany, "We will start to shorten stays"

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
we'll is the contraction of we will

indicators.note: start keeps only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: first letter of shorten

explanation.surface: A German statement promising to cut back on visits.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live or remain there, so it stays in that place.

clue.text: Slapdash hack drawn in by agent

indicators.note: drawn in by means pulled inside, so the first item sits within the second

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
to lop is to hack off

explanation.surface: A careless journalist recruited by a literary agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist, but it is the verb meaning chop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy work is careless and untidy, done hastily with little attention.

clue.text: Releasing secret surrounding power gives a worrying image

indicators.note: surrounding means going around, so the jumbled word encloses the next item
releasing sets the following letters free to fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Leaking secrets about those in power conjures up a frightening prospect.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or a haunting prospect, an apparition that alarms.

clue.text: Nervous about form

parts.note: on means about, concerning
edge is sharpness or form, as when a player loses an edge

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about their form or condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge means being tense and jumpy, unable to relax.

clue.text: Such as Frankenstein — namely one following another one

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for namely
I is the Roman numeral one
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a second Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monster story where one creature is built from another.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein is often counted as the first work of science fiction.

clue.text: Voguish chum is developing

parts.note: in means fashionable
bud is short for buddy, a friend

explanation.surface: A trendy pal is coming along nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant in bud is still forming its flowers, so it is growing and not yet open.

clue.text: Always fresh bit of work on filling flat

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the earlier pieces sit within the last word

parts.note: flat ground is even
an erg is a unit of work in physics
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A small task done on an apartment keeps it looking new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests an apartment but means level. ERG and RE fill EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evergreen stays relevant forever, like a plant that keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Convertible taxi, great success including French article

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the later item sits inside the word before it

parts.note: a riot is a huge hit, as in 'the show was a riot'
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a taxi company boasting about its new convertible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great success' calls for the informal sense of a show or party that was a huge hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, a soft-top automobile.

clue.text: Give a wide berth to a gap

parts.note: taken as written
a void is an empty space or gap

explanation.surface: Steer well clear of an opening, like a sailor near a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a wide berth is an idiom for keeping well away from it, which is to shun it.

clue.text: Those who join without wife could be oldies?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the next item is dropped from the first phrase

parts.note: welders join metal
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Could members who sign up without spouses be pensioners?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those who join' suggests members, but it means WELDERS; drop W.
explanation.definitionFit: Elders are older people, senior members of a family or community.

clue.text: Heartlessly advertise new tranquilliser

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the remaining letters take a different order
heartlessly means without the heart, so the central letter of the next word goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted ad campaign for a new calming drug.
explanation.walkthrough: ADVERTISE loses its middle letter R, and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedative is a drug that calms or induces sleep, so it soothes the patient.
